title: Airbus H125 / AS350 B3e

sources.title: HeliSimmer: Komodo Simulations H125 / AS350 collective
Airbus H125 / AS350 B3e flight manual (public knowledge)
JoyPro function tables MSFS2020/2024 and X-Plane 11/12 (DB/Functions)

intro: The Airbus H125 is a light single-engine helicopter with wide windows. The pilot normally sits in the right seat and flies it with a cyclic stick, a collective lever and two pedals. A computer called FADEC looks after the engine. The panel is compact, and the engine and rotor dials are the most important ones.

areas.name: Instrument panel
areas.text: The compact panel in front of the pilot.

panels.name: Instrument panel
panels.text: The compact panel in front of the pilot with the flight instruments, the engine and vehicle display and the warning lights.
panels.context: The pilot of a helicopter looks at the engine and rotor dials most, because the rotor speed must stay in range.

controls.name: VEMD (vehicle and engine multifunction display)
controls.text: This screen shows engine and helicopter data. At its top is the first limitation indicator (FLI), which combines the most limiting engine values into one reading.
controls.context: The pilot watches it while lifting off and flying to stay within the engine's limits.

controls.name: Airspeed indicator
controls.text: This dial shows how fast the helicopter moves through the air.
controls.context: The pilot watches it during climb, cruise and landing.

controls.name: Attitude indicator
controls.text: This dial shows whether the nose is up or down and whether the helicopter is tilted to a side, like a small model horizon.
controls.context: It is most useful when the real horizon cannot be seen.

controls.name: Altimeter
controls.text: This dial shows the height of the helicopter above sea level.
controls.context: The pilot sets the air-pressure value so that it reads correctly.

controls.name: Rotor / engine rpm indicator (NR / N2)
controls.text: This dial shows how fast the main rotor (NR) and the engine's power turbine (N2) turn.
controls.context: The rotor must turn within a safe range, so the pilot watches this dial all the time.

controls.name: Warning / caution panel
controls.text: This board of labelled lights comes on when something needs attention, and each light has its own label.
controls.context: A light that comes on asks the pilot to check that system.

controls.name: GPS navigator
controls.text: This screen shows the position of the helicopter on a map and helps with navigation.
controls.context: The pilot uses it to find the way.

areas.name: Centre console
areas.text: The console with the engine switch, the fuel shut-off, the rotor brake and the radios.

panels.name: Centre console
panels.text: The console between the seats and below the panel with the engine switch, the fuel shut-off, the rotor brake and the radios.
panels.context: The pilot uses it for starting and stopping the engine.

controls.name: Engine main switch

positions.name: IDLE
positions.text: The engine runs at ground idle after the start.

positions.name: FLIGHT
positions.text: The computer holds the rotor speed; this is the normal setting for flying.

controls.text: This switch starts the engine and chooses how it is controlled. A computer (FADEC) manages the engine and holds the rotor speed in FLIGHT.
controls.context: The pilot moves it from OFF to IDLE for the start, then to FLIGHT.

controls.name: Fuel shut-off lever
controls.text: This lever cuts off the fuel to the engine in an emergency.
controls.context: The pilot uses it only in an emergency.

controls.name: Rotor brake lever
controls.text: This lever brakes the main rotor to a stop after the engine has been shut down.
controls.context: The pilot uses it on the ground after shutdown, so the blades stop sooner.

controls.name: Radio / audio panels
controls.text: These panels set the radio frequencies and choose which radio the pilot talks on.
controls.context: The pilot types the frequency from air traffic control here.

controls.name: Transponder
controls.text: The transponder answers radar so air traffic control can see the helicopter. The pilot sets a four-digit code, called the squawk.
controls.context: Air traffic control tells the pilot which code to set.

areas.name: Overhead panel
areas.text: The switches above the pilot for electricity and lights.

panels.name: Overhead panel
panels.text: The panel above the pilot with the electrical and light switches and the circuit breakers.
panels.context: The pilot uses it while preparing the helicopter.

controls.name: Battery and generator switches
controls.text: These switches connect the battery and the generator to the helicopter's electricity.
controls.context: They are one of the first things switched on.

controls.name: Light switches
controls.text: These switches turn on the lights of the helicopter.
controls.context: The pilot uses them to be seen and to see the ground.

controls.name: Pitot heat
controls.text: This switch heats the pitot tube, the small tube outside that measures speed, so it does not freeze.
controls.context: The pilot uses it in cold and wet air.

controls.name: Circuit breakers
controls.text: Circuit breakers are safety switches that pop out when a system draws too much power. They can be pushed back in.
controls.context: They protect the wiring of the electrical system.

areas.name: Cyclic, collective and pedals
areas.text: The controls the pilot holds or pushes with the feet.

panels.name: Cyclic
panels.text: The cyclic is the stick between the pilot's knees. It tilts the rotor so that the helicopter flies forward, back and sideways.
panels.context: The pilot flies from the right seat, so the right hand holds the cyclic.

controls.name: Cyclic
controls.text: Pushing the cyclic forward makes the helicopter fly forward, pulling back slows it down, and moving it sideways moves the helicopter sideways.
controls.context: The pilot holds it nearly all the time in flight.

controls.name: Trim switch
controls.text: This four-way switch on top of the grip moves the point where the cyclic feels light. The pilot presses it forward, back, left or right.
controls.context: Trim takes away the steady force on the cyclic.

controls.name: Radio / intercom trigger
controls.text: While this trigger on the front of the grip is pressed, the radio transmits.
controls.context: The pilot uses it to talk to air traffic control.

controls.name: Cargo hook release
controls.text: This guarded button releases the load that hangs on the cargo hook below the helicopter.
controls.context: It is pressed to drop a load, so a cover guards it.

panels.name: Collective
panels.text: The collective is the lever at the left of the pilot's seat. It makes the helicopter climb or sink, and has switches on its head.
panels.context: The left hand holds it nearly all the time, and the pedals work together with it.

controls.name: Collective
controls.text: Raising the lever makes all rotor blades bite the air more and the helicopter climbs. Lowering it makes the helicopter sink.
controls.context: The pilot moves it gently, because it changes the load on the engine.

controls.name: Twist grip
controls.text: This twist grip on the collective is a backup way to control the engine fuel by hand. Normally it stays in FLIGHT, where the computer (FADEC) does the job.
controls.context: It is used only if the computer fails and for training.

controls.name: Landing / taxi light switches
controls.text: These switches on the collective head turn the landing light on and off.
controls.context: The pilot uses them without taking a hand off the controls.

controls.name: Hydraulic cut-off switch

positions.name: off
positions.text: The hydraulic boost is off; the controls are heavy.

controls.text: This guarded switch on the collective head turns off the hydraulic boost, the oil pressure that makes the controls light.
controls.context: It is used to test the system or after a failure; without it the controls feel much heavier.

controls.name: Emergency float inflation
controls.text: This spring-guarded button on the collective head inflates the emergency floats on helicopters fitted with them.
controls.context: It is for an emergency landing on water.

panels.name: Anti-torque pedals
panels.text: The pedals at the pilot's feet turn the helicopter's nose to the left or the right.
panels.context: The tail rotor, a small propeller at the tail, stops the helicopter from spinning around, and the pedals change its pitch.

controls.name: Anti-torque pedals
controls.text: Pushing the left or right pedal changes the pitch of the tail rotor blades, which turns the nose to the left or the right.
controls.context: The pilot uses them all the time, especially in a hover.
